**How to use this notebook.** Run one chunk at a time with the green Run arrow (or Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Enter) and look at the output before moving on. Chunks marked **Your turn** are for you to complete; a suggested answer is hidden in a comment underneath.

Our cohort has **only people with epilepsy**: there are no healthy controls. Instead of comparing cases with controls, we will compare **groups of people inside the cohort, defined by their genotype**: for example, people whose epilepsy is explained by a single rare variant against people with no such variant. In this notebook we tidy the clinical data, summarise the genetic findings per person and build those groups.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
source("config.R")
source("R/functions.R")
```

## 1. The clinical table

```{r}
clin_raw <- read_tsv(CLINICAL, show_col_types = FALSE)
glimpse(clin_raw)
```

Real clinical tables are rarely tidy. Before going further, look for problems:

```{r}
count(clin_raw, Sex)
clin_raw %>% filter(is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(`Age at onset (years)`)))) %>% count(`Age at onset (years)`)
```

Three problems: column names with spaces, sex written in five different ways, and age at onset stored as text because some entries say "unknown". Let's fix them.

```{r}
clin <- clin_raw %>%
  rename(IID = `Participant ID`, sex = Sex, onset = `Age at onset (years)`,
         epilepsy_type = `Epilepsy type`, drug_resistant = `Drug resistant`) %>%
  mutate(sex   = case_when(tolower(sex) %in% c("m", "male")   ~ "Male",
                           tolower(sex) %in% c("f", "female") ~ "Female"),
         onset = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(onset)))
count(clin, sex)
summary(clin$onset)
```

## 2. The genetic findings

The diagnostic testing reported rare variants, **one row per variant**. People with no reported variant are simply absent from this table.

```{r}
findings <- read_tsv(FINDINGS, show_col_types = FALSE)
head(findings)
count(findings, acmg)
count(findings, gene, sort = TRUE)
```

Some people have more than one row:

```{r}
findings %>% count(IID) %>% filter(n > 1) %>% left_join(findings, by = "IID")
```

For the analysis we need **one row per person**. Rule: keep the most important finding, Pathogenic first, then Likely pathogenic, then VUS.

```{r}
per_person <- findings %>%
  mutate(rank = match(acmg, c("Pathogenic", "Likely pathogenic", "VUS"))) %>%
  arrange(IID, rank) %>%
  group_by(IID) %>%
  summarise(n_variants  = n(),
            gene        = first(gene),
            consequence = first(consequence),
            acmg        = first(acmg),
            .groups = "drop")
head(per_person)
```

## 3. Define the genotype groups

These are the "case" and "comparison" groups we will use later. Each is a new column.

* **dx_status**: Monogenic (Pathogenic or Likely pathogenic variant), VUS only, or No variant reported.
* **gene_group**: for people with a monogenic diagnosis, whether the gene is usually fully penetrant (almost every carrier has epilepsy) or has incomplete penetrance (many carriers are unaffected). The gene lists are in `config.R`.
* **variant_class**: protein-truncating (PTV) or missense, for monogenic diagnoses.

```{r}
PTV_TERMS <- c("stop_gained", "frameshift_variant", "splice_donor_variant", "splice_acceptor_variant")

groups <- clin %>%
  left_join(per_person, by = "IID") %>%
  mutate(
    dx_status = case_when(acmg %in% c("Pathogenic", "Likely pathogenic") ~ "Monogenic",
                          acmg == "VUS"                                  ~ "VUS only",
                          TRUE                                           ~ "No variant reported"),
    gene_group = case_when(dx_status != "Monogenic"        ~ NA_character_,
                           gene %in% GENES_HIGH_PENETRANCE ~ "High penetrance",
                           gene %in% GENES_INCOMPLETE      ~ "Incomplete penetrance",
                           TRUE                            ~ "Other gene"),
    variant_class = case_when(dx_status != "Monogenic"      ~ NA_character_,
                              consequence %in% PTV_TERMS    ~ "PTV",
                              consequence == "missense_variant" ~ "Missense"))

count(groups, dx_status)
count(groups, dx_status, gene_group, variant_class)
```

## 4. Who has genotypes?

The genotype file (`.fam`) and the clinical table do not always contain the same people. Always check both directions.

```{r}
fam <- read_table(paste0(GENO, ".fam"), col_names = c("FID", "IID", "PAT", "MAT", "SEX", "PHENO"),
                  show_col_types = FALSE)
cat("Genotyped:", nrow(fam), "  In the clinical table:", nrow(groups), "\n")
anti_join(groups, fam, by = "IID") %>% select(IID, epilepsy_type)   # clinical data, no genotypes
anti_join(fam, groups, by = "IID") %>% select(IID)                  # genotypes, no clinical data
```

People without genotypes cannot get a PRS, so they drop out later automatically. Keep a note of the genotyped sample with no clinical record (here an ID ending in `_R`): we will meet it again in the QC notebook.

## 5. A first look

```{r, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4}
p1 <- ggplot(groups, aes(epilepsy_type, fill = dx_status)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GROUP_COLOURS) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "People", fill = NULL, title = "Diagnostic yield by epilepsy type") +
  theme_workshop()
p2 <- groups %>% filter(dx_status == "Monogenic") %>%
  ggplot(aes(forcats::fct_infreq(gene), fill = gene_group)) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = GROUP_COLOURS) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "People", fill = NULL, title = "Monogenic diagnoses by gene") +
  theme_workshop() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
p1 + p2
```
